review_notes:
I read the whole file and the MeanRankUpdate and CorrectionState signatures that bear on the support lemmas. I considered other candidates and left them out because the repeated part is routine or short.
- The three `*_update_on` theorems each rewrite with `barMoment_add_on` twice. That is a thin pattern.
- `barMoment_add_on` and `barMoment_sub_on` are near copies, but each is a thin wrapper around an existing lemma.
- `LocalShell.directional` and `supportedGauge_directional` share a closing step: if f is eventually 0 near p, then fderiv is 0. It is one line (`rw [he.fderiv_eq]` then `simp only [fderiv_fun_const, ...]`), so I judged it too short to extract.
I did not compile anything, so the proposed rewrite is untested. The one finding rests on `angular_supportedGauge` (line 1040) closing by definitional unfolding, as `desired_supportedGauge` does at line 1034. That should work but is unconfirmed.

findings.problem: The desired-axial source has a single slice-level lemma, `desired_slice_support`, which proves that the support of the slice lies in `Icc lo hi` for any bounds `lo`, `hi` below and above the moving patch. Both `desired_supported` (line 610) and `desired_supportedGauge` (line 1034) are one-line corollaries of it. The angular source has no such lemma. `angular_supported` (lines 618–629) and `angular_supportedGauge` (lines 1040–1047) each repeat the same reasoning. Each unfolds to `angularIncrement`, calls `angularIncrement_tsupport` with the same eight arguments, and then reads the two endpoint inequalities off `Ioo` and chains them with the outer bounds. The two copies differ only in the endpoints: `hleft`/`hright` in one, `le_rfl` in the other. This is the same argument as `desired_slice_support` with `angularIncrement` swapped in. The asymmetry makes a reader check two long argument lists by eye, and any change to the `tsupport` lemma's signature must be made in three places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add, next to `desired_slice_support` inside `namespace RankGeometry` (with `include hg`), a mirror lemma:

theorem angular_slice_support (n : ℕ) {x : P} (hx : x ∈ U) {lo hi : ℝ}
    (hlo : lo ≤ r.length n x * r.inner) (hhi : r.length n x * r.outer ≤ hi) :
    support (fun R => CorrectionState.rankAngular r c u n (R, x)) ⊆ Icc lo hi := by
  intro R hR
  change MeanRankUpdate.angularIncrement r.lambda (r.coefficient n x) r.inner r.outer
    (r.length n x) (r.velocity n x) (CorrectionState.debt c u n x) R ≠ 0 at hR
  have h := MeanRankUpdate.angularIncrement_tsupport r.lambda (r.coefficient n x)
    r.inner r.outer (r.velocity n x) (hg.length_pos n x hx) hg.inner_lt_outer
    (CorrectionState.debt c u n x) (subset_tsupport _ hR)
  exact ⟨hlo.trans h.1.le, h.2.le.trans hhi⟩

The proof is that of `desired_slice_support` with `angularIncrement` in place of `desiredAxialIncrement`. Then:

- `angular_supported` becomes `intro p hp hn; exact hg.angular_slice_support n hp (hleft n _ hp) (hright n _ hp) hn`. This is the same shape as `desired_supported`.
- `angular_supportedGauge` becomes `intro p hp hn; exact hg.angular_slice_support n hp le_rfl le_rfl hn`. This is the same shape as `desired_supportedGauge`.

The hypotheses are unchanged. The lemma needs only `hg.length_pos` and `hg.inner_lt_outer`, which `angular_supported` and `angular_supportedGauge` already use. No new imports are required. `potential_supportedGauge` (lines 1049 onward) repeats the same `desiredAxialIncrement_tsupport` call, but it passes `hsupport` to `scaledPrimitive_zero_of_support` unapplied, so I left it out.
findings.benefit: The angular and desired-axial support proofs become parallel, with one place to maintain each unfolding-and-`tsupport` argument. `angular_supported` and `angular_supportedGauge` shrink to one-liners that match `desired_supported` and `desired_supportedGauge`. A reader sees at once that the two sources are handled identically.
